blocks.text: Somewhere between the rise of TikTok and the flood of “get ready with me” tutorials, posing a threat to an entire generation to lose their ability to be bad at something in public as “cringe culture” built the wall. Once just a verb for physical discomfort or embarrassment, “cringe” became a slang term for anything uncool, awkward or embarrassing and it spread from online forums into classrooms, where teachers noticed students growing more self-conscious about visibly putting in effort. A behavior now mocked online as “tryharding.” What changed the stakes was permanence. According to psychologist Aastha Lakhey, a single video or […]...
